key_insight: The paper reframes mini-batch gradient estimation as a survey-sampling problem and uses auxiliary gradient-prediction models to reduce stochastic variance without changing the optimizer itself.
engineering_relevance: This offers a drop-in way to make common training loops like SGD or AdamW more stable and efficient, especially when gradient noise slows convergence or hurts generalization.
method: Treat the training set as a fixed finite population and view mini-batch gradients as sample-based estimators.
Use model-assisted sampling to predict gradients from auxiliary information and build lower-variance estimators.
Retain standard optimizers and dynamics; uniform sampling is recovered as the no-auxiliary-information baseline.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic data and six benchmark datasets reported performance gains in 71–86% of cases, with particularly strong results for medium-sized input spaces and better AdamW generalization in roughly half the training epochs.
watch_item: The added auxiliary prediction model may introduce implementation complexity and its benefit may depend on dataset size and the quality of the auxiliary gradient signal.
paper_title: Stochastic Gradient Optimization with Model-Assisted Sampling
